verses.1: Rely not on your wealth; say not: "I have the power."
verses.2: Rely not on your strength in following the desires of your heart.
verses.3: Say not: "Who can prevail against me?" for the LORD will exact the punishment.
verses.4: Say not: "I have sinned, yet what has befallen me?" for the LORD bides his time.
verses.5: Of forgiveness be not overconfident, adding sin upon sin.
verses.6: Say not: "Great is his mercy; my many sins he will forgive."
verses.7: For mercy and anger alike are with him; upon the wicked alights his wrath.
verses.8: Delay not your conversion to the LORD, put it not off from day to day;
verses.9: For suddenly his wrath flames forth; at the time of vengeance, you will be destroyed.
verses.10: Rely not upon deceitful wealth, for it will be no help on the day of wrath.
verses.11: Winnow not in every wind, and start not off in every direction.
verses.12: Be consistent in your thoughts; steadfast be your words.
verses.13: Be swift to hear, but slow to answer.
verses.14: If you have the knowledge, answer your neighbor; if not, put your hand over your mouth.
verses.15: Honor and dishonor through talking! A man's tongue can be his downfall.
verses.16: Be not called a detractor; use not your tongue for calumny;
verses.17: For shame has been created for the thief, and the reproach of his neighbor for the double-tongued.

notes.text: The vices of the rich are pride and independence (Sirach 5:1-2), presumption (Sirach 5:3), false security (Sirach 5:4-7), and impenitence (Sirach 5:8), which cannot escape the divine wrath (Sirach 5:9, 10). Cf Proverb 18:23; 19:1; 28:6.
A proverbial expression condemning inconstancy and advocating sincerity and honesty.
